newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up 1/4 to 3/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up 1/4 to 3/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose 1/4 to 3/8 of a point by midday as the morning's bond-friendly news on March consumer prices pushed U.S. Treasuries nearly a point higher.

"I guess we are up about 3/8 of a point today just in synch with the government market," one trader said, adding that some bid lists were circulating. "There was a few lists with decent blocks on it, but not an abundance."
The trader cited two lists, which together totaled $200 million, he said.
A second trader said the muni market was "probably up 1/4 to 3/8, (with) a lot of bid lists out, and not a ton of trading."

The Labor Department said March CPI overall rose 0.1 percent, with the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices increasing by 0.2 percent. U.S. economists surveyed by Reuters expected a 0.2 percent rise overall, and a 0.3 percent in the core rate.
In debt futures, the June municipal futures contract was up 25/32 at 112-18/32. The June T-bond contract was up 30/32 at 107-20/32. The MOB spread was 158 ticks.
In the goverment cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 30/32 at 94-8/32 to yield 7.09 percent.
Turning to new issues, Smith Barney Inc said it won $70 million Clark County, Nev., highway revenue improvement bonds at a true interest cost of 5.18 percent.
On the negotiated side, Morgan Stanley & Co said it repriced $30 million New York State Dormitory Authority bonds lowering the top yield in 2026 to 5.93 percent from 5.95 percent.
